A grammar chapter, and a foundational one. It gives you the people-words (pronouns), the fact that Egyptian has no verb "to be" in the present, how gender works, and how to attach "my / your / his" to a noun. Tap any example to reveal its franco and English.

## Personal pronouns

Eight pronouns — note that "you" and "they" distinguish gender in the singular but not the plural.

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| أنا - ana | I |
| إنت - inta | you (m.) |
| إنتِ - inti | you (f.) |
| هو - huwwa | he / it (m.) |
| هي - hiyya | she / it (f.) |
| إحنا - e7na | we |
| إنتو - intu | you (pl.) |
| هم - humma | they |

## The sentence without "to be"

Egyptian has **no present-tense verb "to be"**. You just place the two parts side by side — *I* + *a doctor* — and the "am" is understood.

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا دكتور</summary>
<span class="fr">ana doktor</span>
<span class="en">I'm a doctor (literally just "I doctor")</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>هو مصري</summary>
<span class="fr">huwwa masri</span>
<span class="en">he's Egyptian</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>إحنا من البرازيل</summary>
<span class="fr">e7na men el-Brazil</span>
<span class="en">we're from Brazil</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>البيت كبير</summary>
<span class="fr">el-bet kbeer</span>
<span class="en">the house is big</span>
</details>

To say "is **not**", put **مش (mesh)** in front of the second part:

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا مش جاهز</summary>
<span class="fr">ana mesh gahez</span>
<span class="en">I'm not ready</span>
</details>

(This مش is for non-verb sentences. Negating an actual verb uses the wrapped ما...ش — that's its own grammar chapter.)

## Gender

Almost everything is either masculine or feminine, and it shows up on adjectives:

- A noun ending in **ة (‑a)** is usually feminine: *madrasa* (school), *sa3a* (watch).
- Adjectives agree — the feminine adds **ة**: *kbeer / kbeera* (big), *masri / masreyya* (Egyptian).
- **Countries are feminine:** *masr* (Egypt) takes feminine agreement — *masr 7elwa* "Egypt is beautiful".

## Possessive endings

To say "my house", you don't use a separate word — you glue an ending onto the noun. Here they all are on **بيت (bet)** "house":

| Ending - franco | Meaning | On بيت |
|---|---|---|
| ـي - ‑i | my | بيتي - beti |
| ـك - ‑ak | your (m.) | بيتك - betak |
| ـك - ‑ek | your (f.) | بيتك - betek |
| ـه - ‑o | his | بيته - beto |
| ـها - ‑ha | her | بيتها - betha |
| ـنا - ‑na | our | بيتنا - betna |
| ـكو - ‑ko | your (pl.) | بيتكو - betko |
| ـهم - ‑hom | their | بيتهم - bethom |

A feminine noun ending in **ة** turns that ة into a **‑t‑** before the ending: **عربية (3arabeyya)** "car" → **عربيتي (3arabeyti)** "my car", **عربيتك (3arabeytak)** "your car".

There's also an alternative way to say "mine / yours" with the word **بتاع (betaa3)** — *el-bet da bta3i* "this house is mine" — covered in the *This and That* chapter.

## Examples

<details class="frase">
<summary>ده بيتي</summary>
<span class="fr">da beti</span>
<span class="en">this is my house</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>عربيتها حمرا</summary>
<span class="fr">3arabeytha 7amra</span>
<span class="en">her car is red</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>إنت مصري؟</summary>
<span class="fr">inta masri?</span>
<span class="en">are you (m.) Egyptian?</span>
</details>

**1.** we

<span class="fr">e7na</span>
</details>

**2.** they

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>

<span class="fr">humma</span>
</details>

**3.** you (f.)

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">إنتِ</span>
<span class="fr">inti</span>
</details>

### Exercise 2 — Add the possessive ending

Attach the ending to بيت (*bet*, house).

**1.** his house

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">بيته</span>
<span class="fr">beto</span>
</details>

**2.** our house

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">بيتنا</span>
<span class="fr">betna</span>
</details>

**3.** their house

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">بيتهم</span>
<span class="fr">bethom</span>
</details>

</details>

<details class="ans">

**3.** I'm not ready.
